items.title: 61428_Red Callender oral history interview
items.q: Jack Lauderdale owned the label, and Lloyd Glenn was his featured artist, and Lloyd Glenn sold a lot of records for them.

ctx.x: Imperial. The Imperial label. I was the A&R man. I think this was the early Fifties. Yeah, this was in the early Fifties before I started working for (Down Beat, not IMPERIAL). Dolphin. Jack Lauderdale owned the label, and Lloyd Glenn was his featured artist, and Lloyd Glenn sold a lot of records for them. As a matter of fact, he made them a lot of money.

Anyway, I was going to tell a story about he and I taking a trip to St. Louis to see Jimmy Forrest, on Clark Terry's recommendation. So we get to St. Louis, and we go hear Jimmy Forrest, and I wanted to buy him right away. Because he was playing "Happy Go Lucky Local" which later became "Night Train". Remember that?
